subject: Order form proration & implementation buffer — proposed amendment
messages:
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@bufferly.com>, procurement@bufferly.com
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form proration & implementation buffer — proposed amendment

Elena / procurement team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. To make sure Bufferly has the headroom they asked for during holiday traffic spikes, we've put together a short amendment that: 1) adds a 10% burst buffer (non-guaranteed capacity) that can be used at Redistributed rates, and 2) includes a monthly proration approach for any mid-term capacity top-ups so invoices align with usage.

I've attached a redline (Bufferly_Amendment_REDLINE_v1.pdf) that shows the proposed Exhibit and Order Form edits. Key asks:
- Can procurement confirm whether Bufferly needs a firm committed top-up or the non-guaranteed buffer is sufficient?
- Legal question: if we include a 10% burst buffer, do we need an explicit rollback safeguard in the MSA or is the Order Form exhibit enough?
- Billing: if we prorate mid-month, Bufferly prefers a per-day proration rather than rounding to the month — any operational constraints?

Next steps: if this looks ok, can you provide a procurement redline back by EOD Tuesday so our legal and billing teams can reconcile? If you prefer a short call to walk the redline, Marcus and I are available Wed afternoon.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Bufferly_Amendment_REDLINE_v1.pdf, OrderForm_Bufferly_v2.xlsx

From: Elena Torres <elena@bufferly.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, procurement@bufferly.com
Cc: Harry Cho <harry.cho@bufferly.com>
Date: 2025-09-15T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form proration & implementation buffer — proposed amendment

Karthik —

Appreciate the quick turn. Procurement reviewed the redline and we have three immediate concerns:

1) Fee proration: Our procurement policy requires any mid-term billing adjustments to be prorated to the invoice day level but with a maximum of 5 business days to reflect on billing systems. Your proposed immediate per-day proration is acceptable but will need billing reconciliation notes.

2) Rollback / rollback safeguard: We cannot accept language that allows Redwood to unilaterally reduce committed capacity without a 30-day advance notice and a right to cure. Bufferly needs an explicit rollback safeguard in the MSA.

3) SLA fallback: During burst events we need clear SLA fallback definitions (e.g., degraded throughput thresholds and incident response times).

I've attached our procurement redline (Bufferly_Procurement_Redline_0915.pdf). We'd like Redwood legal to propose compromise language for rollback and SLA fallback.

If you can send suggested contract language by Friday, we can route to our legal and procurement for sign-off.

—Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Procurement, Bufferly Inc
elena@bufferly.com

Date: 2025-09-16T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Order form proration & implementation buffer — please advise (internal)

Team —

Looping you in on Bufferly's procurement redline (attached). Procurement is asking for a 30-day rollback notice and a billing reconciliation window of up to 5 business days for proration. They also want explicit SLA fallback thresholds for burst events.

Proposed approach (quick):
- Commit to the 10% non-guaranteed burst buffer as an Order Form exhibit but add an explicit rollback safeguard in the MSA (30-day notice + 10-day cure period for capacity disputes).
- Accept per-day proration operationally but include billing reconciliation notes and a 5-business-day processing window. Naomi — can billing support that window?
- Marcus — can you draft the SLA fallback bullet points we can include in the exhibit (throughput % degradation, incident response SLAs, and escalation contact)?
- Jonas / Legal — please propose concise language for the rollback safeguard and confirm whether the MSA or Order Form is the better place to memorialize it. If we can prepare a clean counter with those updates, we should push to DocuSign and aim for signature by 9/22 to lock Q4 tags.

Attached: proposed_amendment_v2.docx (I merged procurement feedback inline).

Thanks —
Karthik

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@bufferly.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-18T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form proration & implementation buffer — proposed amendment (legal counter)

Elena / Karthik —

Thanks for the clear notes, Elena. See attached a focused legal counter with suggested language for rollback and an SLA fallback exhibit (Redline_MSA_with_Rollback_Clause.pdf). Summary of the legal position:

1) Rollback safeguard: Redwood can include an MSA rollback clause that allows us to reduce committed capacity in exceptional circumstances (hardware deprecation, region outage, model deprecation) but only with 30 days' notice and a 10-day cure period during which Bufferly may purchase temporary burst credits at mutually agreed rates. That preserves operational flexibility while giving Bufferly a right to cure.

2) Proration / billing window: We accept per-day proration with a 5-business-day maximum processing window included in the billing exhibit. We'll add a reconciliation paragraph describing how adjustments are reflected on monthly invoices and credits.

3) SLA fallback: Marcus and I worked with the SRE playbook to propose fallback thresholds: degraded throughput = 25% below baseline for >15 minutes triggers priority incident; response within 2 hours for Sev 1, 24-hour remediation SLA for sustained degradation. These are in the exhibit.

If Bufferly accepts this language, we'll prepare a clean order form and push to DocuSign. Laura / Naomi — can you confirm the billing flow and signatory list so we can populate the DocuSign envelope? Elena — please let us know if Bufferly needs additional procurement counters; otherwise we aim to send a DocuSign envelope by 9/19.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Attachments: Redline_MSA_with_Rollback_Clause.pdf
